entries.name: 710GO
entries.stage: Sponsor-reported first dosing in Phase 1; Australian oral-peptide study
entries.summary: Kalohexis describes 710GO as an oral peptide acting at both melanocortin-3 and melanocortin-4 receptors. Its 28 May 2026 announcement reports first dosing in a randomized, placebo-controlled Australian Phase 1 study, with planned single-dose, multiple-dose and food-effect assessments in approximately 100 healthy volunteers with overweight or obesity.
entries.ukAuthorisation: The reviewed sponsor evidence does not establish UK marketing authorisation or UK clinical-trial authorisation for 710GO.
entries.nhsEngland: No NICE recommendation or NHS England access is established by the reviewed evidence.
entries.supply: Australian research and sponsor-reported first dosing do not establish lawful UK retail supply, pharmacy stock or sale by Shift Some Timber.
entries.limitations: First dosing is sponsor-reported. Approximately 100 participants is planned enrolment, not an actual recruitment count. The announcement contains no human trial results or verified completion date. Its weight, fat, lean-mass, tolerability, post-treatment maintenance and semaglutide-combination observations concern preclinical studies, including non-human primates; they do not establish human efficacy, safety, muscle strength or function, durability, superiority or an approved regimen. Exact-name and sponsor ClinicalTrials.gov searches returned no matching public record in this pass; registry discovery remains incomplete rather than proof that no study exists. The separate mifomelatide cancer-cachexia programme is not obesity evidence.
